To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is possible to encode object oriented classes within Haskell and to use object-oriented class libraries from within Haskell.

(a) Haskell has a sophisticated type system that can be extended with closed classes and overlapping instances, (b) the extended system is powerful enough to support the encoding of object-oriented programming in Haskell, (c) the extended system can be implemented efficiently, (d) the extended system has been used in practice to implement a large number of object-oriented class libraries for Haskell.

(i) Haskell's type system can be extended so as to support object-oriented style overloading; (ii) the resulting type system can be used to encode object-oriented class libraries in Haskell; (iii) object-oriented class libraries can be easily imported and used within Haskell.
